answer:
FedAvg averages client updates, usually weighted by participating clients' sample counts. With non-IID data, several local steps move each client toward its own objective and can produce client drift. FedProx adds $\frac\mu2\|w-w_t\|^2$ to each client's objective, discouraging excessive departure from the current global model. SCAFFOLD uses client/server control variates to correct update directions. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05629) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06127) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.06378)

Tune local steps, learning rate, participation, and proximal strength under realistic heterogeneity and stragglers. Compare global accuracy with worst-client and subgroup performance, communication rounds, and compute. Averaging is not automatically privacy-preserving: gradients can leak information. Secure aggregation and properly accounted differential privacy address distinct threats, and neither eliminates statistical heterogeneity or guarantees every client benefits equally.
